'''Isde Naha''' an [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] located in the [[Greater Javin/Legends|Greater Javin]] region. An [[Factory world/Legends|industrial world]] with no tolerance toward law-breaking and [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]], it was originally [[Colonist/Legends|settled]] as part of the [[Javin sector/Legends|Javin sector]]. Around [[400 BBY/Legends|400 BBY]], the portion of that [[Sector/Legends|sector]] containing Isde Naha became the new [[Anoat sector/Legends|Anoat sector]], and, generations later, it in turn was re-designated the [[Yarith sector/Legends|Yarith sector]], which the planet served as the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of. Isde Naha hosted a significant presence of the [[Figg conglomerate|corporate interests]] of the Greater Javin's influential [[Figg family]], and, after a series of [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] raids during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] that resulted in the seizure of [[Figg Excavations/Legends|Figg Excavations]] [[Transport/Legends|transports]], the [[Mining Guild/Legends|Mining Guild's]] [[Guild Enforcers|Enforcer]] [[Fannis Gult]] coordinated the Guild's investigation efforts into the matter from Isde Naha.

==Description==
Isde Naha was a terrestrial<ref name="Rough" /> [[Planet/Legends|planet]]<ref name="GG" /> located in the [[Isde Naha system/Legends|Isde Naha system]], a part of the [[Yarith sector/Legends|Yarith sector]]. It was situated in the [[Greater Javin/Legends|Greater Javin]] region, a part of the [[Western Reaches/Legends|Western Reaches]] portion of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. Isde Naha lay on the [[Super-hyperroute/Legends|super-hyperroute]] known as the [[Corellian Trade Spine/Legends|Corellian Trade Spine]], which linked it to the [[Togominda system/Legends|Togominda system]] and the neighboring [[Anoat sector/Legends|Anoat sector's]] [[Ozu system/Legends|Ozu system]], while the [[Lipsec Run/Legends|Lipsec Run]] [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlane]] connected it to the [[Bettel system/Legends|Bettel system]] as well as the [[Abridon system/Legends|Abridon system]]<ref name="TEA" /> of the [[Kriz sector/Legends|Kriz sector]].<ref name="EAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref>

==History==
===Early explorations===
[[Realspace/Legends|Space]] surrounding Isde Naha was [[Scout/Legends|explored]] by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] between [[3000 BBY]] and [[1000 BBY/Legends|1000 BBY]], with the planet being situated in territory under the control of members of the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] tradition of [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-users]] between [[1004 BBY]] and 1000 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]], during the [[Light and Darkness War|final phase]] of their [[Millennium/Legends|millennium]]-long [[New Sith Wars|conflict]] against the Republic.<ref name="TEA" /> After the Republic's victory in a [[Galactic Republic–Mugaari war|war]] against the nearby civilization of the [[Mugaari]] [[Species/Legends|species]]<ref name="GG" /> at some point between approximately 1000 BBY and [[600 BBY/Legends|600 BBY]],<ref name="MugaariDate">{{RepublicMugaariWarDate}}</ref> the former established the [[Javin sector/Legends|Javin sector]] in the former [[Mugaari Space/Legends|Mugaari Space]]. There, launching from newly [[Colonist/Legends|colonized]] worlds such as Isde Naha, Republic [[Merchant/Legends|merchants]] unsuccessfully attempted to discover shortcut trade routes through the region's [[Twin Nebulae/Legends|Twin Nebulae]]&mdash;the [[Ivax Nebula/Legends|Ivax]] and [[Kiax Nebula/Legends|Kiax Nebula]]&mdash;that would better connect the civilizations of the [[Alien/Legends|alien]] [[Lutrillian/Legends|Lutrillians]] and [[Nothoiin/Legends|Nothoiins]] to the wider [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]. Such hyperlanes were ultimately established through the efforts of the entrepreneur [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] [[Ecclessis Figg/Legends|Ecclessis Figg]].<ref name="GG" />

===Figg history===
[[File:EcclessisFiggStatue-JoY.png|thumb|right|300px|Lord Ecclessis Figg (statue pictured) played an important role in Isde Naha's history.]]
Figg's achievements in the exploration of the region also included the blazing of a [[Nothoiin Route|new route]] that connected the [[Nothoiin Corridor]] hyperlane to<ref name="GG" /> the Lipsec Run<ref name="TEA" />&mdash;and therefore eventually to the Corellian Trade Spine at Isde Naha. The discovery accelerated the development of the more backwater areas of the Javin [[Sector/Legends|sector]]. In the last [[Standard year/Legends|year]] of Figg's life,<ref name="GG" /> around [[400 BBY/Legends|400 BBY]],<ref name="SectorDates" /> the portion of the sector containing Isde Naha was re-designated as the new Anoat sector, and generations after that, the Anoat itself was further split into two parts, with Isde Naha becoming a part of the Yarith sector.<ref name="GG" /> Although Isde Naha lay outside the Republic's borders during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]],<ref name="TEA" /> during the first campaigns of that conflict in [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], the Republic's [[Nineteenth Army|Nineteenth Sector Army]] was nevertheless tasked with engaging the [[Confederacy military/Legends|military forces]] of the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] in the planet's vicinity.<ref name="EGTW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' &mdash; Based on corresponding data for [[Isde Naha system/Legends|Isde Naha system]]</ref>

At some point during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] between the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]]&mdash;not long after the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]]<ref name="Rough" /> of [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]]<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref>&mdash;the [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] [[Clabburn the Younger]] and [[Salmakk]] launched a series of raids in the Greater Javin, capturing several raw material [[Transport/Legends|transports]] of the local company [[Figg Excavations/Legends|Figg Excavations]]. Due to it already harboring suspicions about the company's loyalty, the [[Mining Guild/Legends|Mining Guild]], of which Figg Excavations was a member, launched a security investigation into the matter, dispatching a team of its paramilitary [[Guild Enforcers]] to the region. Due to their relative unfamiliarity with the area, the Enforcers were forced to set up a temporary office on<ref name="Rough" /> the nearby planet<ref name="GG" /> [[Darlyn Boda/Legends|Darlyn Boda]] in order to recruit local [[Spacer/Legends|spacers]] to help locate the pirates, with the Guild's team wishing for the raiders to be delivered to [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|law enforcement officials]] on Isde Naha for questioning. The leader of the Enforcer team, [[Fannis Gult]], was also based on Isde Naha, though her impatience motivated her to leave that world and be more directly involved in the investigation.<ref name="Rough" />

==Inhabitants==
Isde Naha was an extremely rigid<ref name="GG" /> [[Factory world/Legends|industrialized world]] that served as the Yarith sector's [[Capital/Legends|capital]].<ref name="TEA" /> It had strict regulations<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|118|Isde Naha}}</ref> and lacked any tolerance toward law-breaking and [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]].<ref name="TEA" /> The finance and engineering sectors of Isde Naha featured a heavy presence of the Greater Javin's influential [[Figg conglomerate|corporate interests]] controlled by the [[Figg family|descendants]] of Ecclessis Figg,<ref name="GG" /> with the world being proud of its Figg heritage. The population of the Isde Naha [[Star system/Legends|system]] around [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]] numbered between one and ten billion.<ref name="TEA" />

==Behind the scenes==
Isde Naha was introduced in [[Wizards of the Coast]]'s ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]'' supplements "[[Galactic Gazetteer: Hoth and the Greater Javin]]"<ref name="GG" /> and "[[Rough and Tundra]]," both of which where published on [[Wizards.com]] on [[March 25]], [[2004]].<ref name="Rough" /> The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed Isde Naha in grid square K-18.<ref name="TEA" />
